purpose: Add eight more source-exact Isaac Watts hymn stanzas for sermon preparation and presentation slides.

defaults.author: Isaac Watts
defaults.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the stanza is verified against the stored text.

entries.title: Run the heavenly race
entries.text:
Awake, our souls, away, our fears,
Let every trembling thought be gone;
Awake and run the heavenly race,
And put a cheerful courage on.
entries.slideText:
Awake and run the heavenly race,
And put a cheerful courage on.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed opening stanza for messages about perseverance, courage, and running the Christian race.
entries.reviewNote: This is hymn poetry, not Scripture. Define the race and its strength from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Beauties in my Saviour
entries.text:
When strangers stand and hear me tell
What beauties in my Saviour dwell;
Where he is gone, they fain would know,
That they may seek and love him too.
entries.slideText: What beauties in my Saviour dwell
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed poetic invitation to speak of Christ winsomely and direct hearers to Him.
entries.reviewNote: The Song of Solomon connection is Watts's devotional application. Establish every claim about Christ from clear KJV passages.

entries.title: Why do we mourn departing friends
entries.text:
Why do we mourn departing friends
Or shake at death's alarms?
'Tis but the voice that Jesus sends
To call them to his arms.
entries.slideText:
Why do we mourn departing friends
Or shake at death's alarms?
entries.recommendedUse: Use carefully as an attributed funeral or memorial stanza after establishing the believer's hope from Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: Apply only to those whose profession gives biblical grounds for Christian hope. Do not let poetic consolation replace the KJV text or sensitive pastoral care.

entries.title: At the great rising day
entries.text:
Then let the last loud trumpet sound,
And bid our kindred rise,
Awake, ye nations under ground,
Ye saints, ascend the skies.
entries.slideText:
Then let the last loud trumpet sound,
And bid our kindred rise
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed resurrection stanza in funeral, Second Coming, or Easter preaching.
entries.reviewNote: The stanza compresses prophetic imagery. Explain the resurrection and Christ's return from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Alas! and did my Saviour bleed
entries.text:
Alas! and did my Saviour bleed,
And did my Sovereign die?
Would he devote that sacred head
For such a worm as I?
entries.slideText:
Alas! and did my Saviour bleed,
And did my Sovereign die?
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed cross-centered stanza for Good Friday, Communion, or Gospel preaching.
entries.reviewNote: The self-description is poetic humility. Present human dignity, sin, and Christ's atoning death from the cited KJV texts.

entries.title: Amazing pity! grace unknown!
entries.text:
Was it for crimes that I had done
He groan'd upon the tree?
Amazing pity! grace unknown!
And love beyond degree!
entries.slideText:
Amazing pity! grace unknown!
And love beyond degree!
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed response stanza after explaining Christ's substitutionary death from Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: This is poetic meditation. The nature and sufficiency of the atonement must be established from the governing KJV passages.

entries.title: My God, my life, my love
entries.text:
My God, my life, my love,
To thee, to thee I call,
I cannot live if thou remove,
For thou art all in all.
entries.slideText:
My God, my life, my love,
To thee, to thee I call
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed devotional stanza in messages about desiring God and resting in His presence.
entries.reviewNote: This is personal devotional language. Keep the application rooted in the cited KJV passages and the believer's union with Christ.

entries.title: The wings of faith
entries.text:
Give me the wings of faith to rise
Within the veil, and see
The saints above, how great their joys,
How bright their glories be.
entries.slideText:
Give me the wings of faith to rise
Within the veil, and see
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed poetic transition when preaching about faithful witnesses and the believer's heavenly hope.
entries.reviewNote: The imagery is poetic. Avoid speculation about the intermediate state and teach from the cited KJV passages.
